title: RAD 112 - Radiographic Positioning and Modern Imaging Modalities

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Hounsfield unit?
o: imaging that uses high frequency sound waves to show soft tissue
the scale value that expresses the density of a tissue on a CT image
the ring that holds the tube and detectors and rotates around the patient
the confirmation of a patient's identity before any examination begins
items.s: Hounsfield unit: the scale value that expresses the density of a tissue on a CT image. The other options describe Gantry, Patient identification, Ultrasound.

items.s: Doppler mode: the setting that shows the flow of blood through vessels. The other options describe Repeat exposure, Contrast medium, Manual handling.

items.s: Supine: the position in which the patient lies on the back. The other options describe Anteroposterior, Patient positioning, Central ray.

items.s: Thoracic cavity: the space enclosed by the ribs that contains the heart and lungs. The other options describe Manual handling, Dose monitoring, Radiofrequency pulse.

items.q: The statement “the respect shown by covering the patient and limiting unnecessary exposure” describes which of the following?

items.q: In this course, Communication refers to
o: the safe technique used to move a patient without injuring anyone
the clear explanation of a procedure given in words the patient understands
the trolley of resuscitation equipment kept ready for a collapsed patient
the respect shown by covering the patient and limiting unnecessary exposure
items.s: Communication: the clear explanation of a procedure given in words the patient understands. The other options describe Manual handling, Dignity, Emergency trolley.

Image processing

Look-up table

items.q: The correct meaning of Cephalad angulation is
o: a projection in which the beam enters the front and exits the back
the middle of the beam that is aimed at the point of interest
a projection in which the beam enters the back and exits the front
a tube tilt in which the beam is directed toward the patient's head
items.s: Cephalad angulation: a tube tilt in which the beam is directed toward the patient's head. The other options describe Anteroposterior, Posteroanterior, Central ray.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Contrast medium?

an unwanted response of the patient to the contrast medium
the agreement given after the risks of a procedure are explained
a soluble medium containing iodine used for vessels and urinary studies
items.s: Contrast medium: a substance given to make a structure stand out on the image. The other options describe Iodinated contrast, Adverse reaction, Informed consent.

items.q: “an unwanted response of the patient to the contrast medium” is the definition of
o: Contrast medium
Negative contrast
Adverse reaction
Iodinated contrast

Computed tomography
Magnetic resonance imaging

the ability of an image to show small structures lying close together
loss of density at the image edges from incorrect grid alignment
any feature on the image that is not part of the patient's anatomy
items.s: Grid cut-off: loss of density at the image edges from incorrect grid alignment. The other options describe Spatial resolution, Artefact, Noise.

items.q: “the position in which the patient lies on the back” is the definition of
o: Decubitus

Supine

items.q: In this course, Pelvic girdle refers to
o: the bones that support the body and are seen on most radiographs
the ring of bones that supports the trunk and protects pelvic organs
the space below the diaphragm that holds the digestive organs
the space enclosed by the ribs that contains the heart and lungs
items.s: Pelvic girdle: the ring of bones that supports the trunk and protects pelvic organs. The other options describe Skeletal system, Thoracic cavity, Abdominal cavity.

the tilting of the tube or part away from the perpendicular
the middle of the beam that is aimed at the point of interest
a projection in which the beam enters the front and exits the back

a tube tilt in which the beam is directed toward the patient's head

the middle of the beam that is aimed at the point of interest
the tilting of the tube or part away from the perpendicular
the path the central ray takes through the part being examined

items.q: The correct meaning of Nuclear spin is
o: the burst of energy that disturbs the alignment of nuclei in a scanner
the property of hydrogen nuclei that makes magnetic resonance possible
imaging that uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves to show tissue
the scale value that expresses the density of a tissue on a CT image
items.s: Nuclear spin: the property of hydrogen nuclei that makes magnetic resonance possible. The other options describe Magnetic resonance imaging, Radiofrequency pulse, Hounsfield unit.

items.q: In this course, Lateral refers to

the upright stance with palms forward that all descriptions refer to
the position in which the patient lies on one side
a position in which the patient lies on a side using a horizontal beam
items.s: Lateral: the position in which the patient lies on one side. The other options describe Oblique, Decubitus, Anatomical position.

a substance given to make a structure stand out on the image

the routine checking of the radiation received by staff and patients

an unwanted response of the patient to the contrast medium
an insoluble medium used to outline the digestive tract
a substance given to make a structure stand out on the image

imaging that uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves to show tissue
the property of hydrogen nuclei that makes magnetic resonance possible
items.s: Computed tomography: imaging that builds cross-sectional pictures from many X-ray projections. The other options describe Nuclear spin, Magnetic resonance imaging, Radiofrequency pulse.

describing a structure that returns no echoes and appears black

items.s: Ultrasound: imaging that uses high frequency sound waves to show soft tissue. The other options describe Anechoic, Hyperechoic, Echo.
